extracted.intended_audience: health insurance issuers, plan administrators, covered entities and recipients of Federal financial assistance subject to Section 1557 (OCR), plus their legal/compliance advisors and advocates
extracted.subtask_description: Preamble and responses in HHS OCR's final Section 1557 rule describing nondiscrimination standards and enforcement expectations for health plan benefit design, marketing, cost sharing, formularies, provider networks, and related practices. Focuses on what conduct may constitute prohibited discrimination and how OCR will analyze claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on discriminatory cost sharing and coverage limitations (§92.207(b)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Covered entities are prohibited from “impos[ing] additional cost sharing or other limitations or restrictions on coverage, on the basis of race, color, national origin, sex, age, or disability.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR clarifies it does not dictate business decisions about what cost sharing to impose, but whatever cost sharing an issuer imposes cannot be applied in a discriminatory manner. Comments about Essential Health Benefits (EHB) fall outside this rule's scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on discriminatory marketing practices (§92.207(b)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Marketing practices that are designed or implemented in a way that discriminates against individuals with a disability or on any other prohibited basis are prohibited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inaccuracies or omissions that were intended to or resulted in discouraging individuals from enrolling, or steering individuals away from coverage on a prohibited basis, would raise discrimination concerns. Determination is fact-specific and case-by-case; OCR declined to specify particular regulatory examples but referenced an example from the Proposed Rule (e.g., avoiding advertising in areas populated by a majority of people of color). OCR also notes other Federal/Departmental marketing rules may apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notices and accessibility measures to address marketing and access (§§92.10, 92.11, 92.201, 92.202)
rubrics_metrics.description: Covered entities must provide a Notice of Nondiscrimination and Notice of Availability and take reasonable steps to provide meaningful access to individuals with LEP and ensure effective communication for individuals with disabilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR identified specific regulatory provisions (Notice of Nondiscrimination §92.10; Notice of Availability under §92.11, including member handbook requirements; meaningful access §92.201; effective communication §92.202) as measures to mitigate marketing and access barriers for LEP individuals and those with disabilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on discriminatory health plan benefit design (§92.207(b)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Covered entities are explicitly prohibited from having or implementing benefit designs that discriminate on any protected basis under §92.207(b)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR declined to define the term “benefit design” in regulatory text to avoid being overly prescriptive and inconsistent with other Departmental regulations. Nevertheless, benefit design features may result in discriminatory denial of access to medically necessary care, particularly for individuals with disabilities who have significant health needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples of benefit design features (non-exhaustive)
rubrics_metrics.description: For purposes of applying Section 1557, examples include, but are not limited to: coverage, exclusions, and limitations of benefits; prescription drug formularies; cost sharing (copays, coinsurance, deductibles); utilization management techniques (step therapy, prior authorization); medical management standards (medical necessity); provider network design; reimbursement rates; and standards for provider admission to participate in a network.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR lists these as illustrative features of benefit design that can be evaluated for discriminatory effect, while emphasizing fact-specific inquiries rather than per se rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: OCR will not provide presumptively discriminatory benefit design lists; fact-specific inquiries required
rubrics_metrics.description: OCR declines to provide a non-exhaustive list of presumptively discriminatory benefit design examples in the final rule and declines to import presumptively discriminatory examples from CMS's EHB regulations into this rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determinations that a particular benefit design is discriminatory will be made on a case-by-case basis using fact-intensive analysis consistent with civil rights principles and relevant case law. OCR may consider issuing future guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Potentially discriminatory prescription drug formulary practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain formulary practices could raise discrimination concerns, including placing most or all drugs treating a particular condition into the highest cost-sharing tier; excluding single-tablet regimens even when they are the standard of care; requiring use of specialty pharmacy programs that mandate mail delivery; and applying quantity limits for an entire drug class without scientific or clinical explanation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR declines to declare specific practices per se discriminatory; instead, these practices are raised as examples that could be investigated. OCR also notes some nondiscriminatory formulary tools (e.g., preferred drug lists) remain permissible if coverage criteria are not discriminatory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coverage of physician-administered (“medical benefit”) drugs treated as benefit design
rubrics_metrics.description: Coverage decisions for physician-administered medical benefit drugs are considered part of a plan's benefit design and subject to Section 1557 review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR will investigate such coverage practices on a case-by-case basis for potential discrimination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissibility of nondiscriminatory utilization management and formulary practices
rubrics_metrics.description: The rule does not prohibit covered entities from engaging in nondiscriminatory utilization management techniques or formulary design.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of permissible practices include preferred drug lists under Medicaid, provided the coverage criteria do not constitute prohibited discrimination. OCR will assess whether utilization management is applied in a nondiscriminatory manner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on categorical exclusions of services related to gender transition or gender-affirming care (§92.207(b)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicit, categorical exclusions or limitations of coverage for all health services related to gender transition or other gender-affirming care impermissibly single out an entire category of services based on an individual's transgender status and are presumptively discriminatory on the basis of sex.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR treats categorical exclusions for gender-affirming care as presumptively discriminatory and declined to accept comments arguing this undercuts the regulation. This provision is discussed alongside §92.206 which addresses gender-affirming care.

rubrics_metrics.name: Blanket exclusions or limitations tied to a specific disability raise significant concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: A coverage limitation or exclusion that is based on a specific disability or condition (e.g., blanket exclusions for ASD services, exclusions of hearing-loss treatments other than cochlear implants, unique annual caps on wheelchairs) would be investigated as potentially discriminatory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR expects covered entities to provide legitimate, nondiscriminatory reasons for such exclusions. The rule does not require coverage of all services related to a disability; rather, exclusions will be evaluated case-by-case and courts have in some cases rejected proxy-discrimination claims regarding certain exclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Habilitative vs rehabilitative coverage parity considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Commenters raised that limits on habilitative services and devices that are more restrictive than for rehabilitative services may discriminate against people with disabilities needing habilitation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR notes CMS EHB regulations require coverage of habilitative services and prohibit less favorable limits on habilitative services and devices than on rehabilitative ones; OCR will assess coverage limitations under Section 1557 principles and relevant Departmental authorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reimbursement rates and integration provision (§92.207(b)(6))
rubrics_metrics.description: Reimbursement rates and related policies are part of a plan's benefit design and must be provided in a nondiscriminatory manner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR will examine complaints alleging less favorable treatment in reimbursement for mental health or other services compared to physical health services on a case-by-case basis; such matters also relate to integration provisions discussed elsewhere in the rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Age-related distinctions must be analyzed under the Age Act and Section 1557
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 1557 prohibits discrimination on the basis of age consistent with the Age Act, which permits certain age distinctions under specified circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When investigating an age-based benefit design, OCR will first determine whether the distinction is permitted under the Age Act. If not permitted, OCR will then investigate whether the age distinction violates Section 1557. Covered entities must provide legitimate, nondiscriminatory justifications for age distinctions; the rule does not require coverage of all services for all ages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Covered entities must submit Assurance of Compliance (§92.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients of Federal financial assistance (including issuers) are required to submit an Assurance of Compliance attesting they will not discriminate on prohibited bases including age.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR declined to require a separate pediatric attestation; the existing Assurance of Compliance is the attestation mechanism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training requirement for relevant employees (§92.9)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 92.9 requires covered entities to provide training to relevant employees on their Section 1557 Policies and Procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR emphasized it is in covered entities' best interest to ensure staff are adequately trained but declined to specify additional training content or requirements at this time. Covered entities remain responsible for ensuring staff, subrecipients, and subcontractors comply with Section 1557.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defense standard under §92.207(c): legitimate, nondiscriminatory reason
rubrics_metrics.description: Covered entities may raise a defense under §92.207(c) by asserting a legitimate, nondiscriminatory basis for a coverage limitation that might otherwise appear discriminatory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When investigating, OCR will consider whether the covered entity's justification is legitimate and not a pretext for discrimination. If legitimate, OCR will conclude the challenged design feature is not prohibited under the rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proxy discrimination and disparate-impact theories are available enforcement tools
rubrics_metrics.description: Proxy discrimination (policies neutral on their face but closely associated with a protected group) and disparate impact theories are among the civil rights theories OCR may use in Section 1557 investigations and enforcement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR declined to expressly include the proxy discrimination theory in the rule text because of the fact-intensive nature of such analyses, but notes courts have applied these theories in Section 1557 cases and OCR will evaluate such claims on a case-by-case basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Case-by-case Benefit Design Analysis and enforcement process (see §92.301)
rubrics_metrics.description: OCR's determinations regarding whether a particular benefit design is discriminatory will be fact-specific, conducted on a case-by-case basis, consistent with longstanding civil rights principles and relevant case law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR will utilize all applicable causes of action when investigating potential discrimination under Section 1557. The process will weigh the covered entity's stated reasons, examine whether they are pretextual, and may involve coordination with other Departmental authorities when relevant (e.g., CMS EHB rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reproductive health services coverage must be nondiscriminatory if offered
rubrics_metrics.description: To the extent plans cover infertility diagnosis, treatment, assisted reproductive technology, contraception, or abortion services, coverage must be provided on a nondiscriminatory basis (including with respect to sexual orientation, gender identity, sex characteristics, or relationship status).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR declined to enumerate every reproductive service in regulatory text, reasoning the general prohibition on discriminatory limitations (§92.207(b)(1)) applies. OCR also noted denying access to medications that may be used for abortion purposes when prescribed for non-abortion reasons may constitute discrimination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Religious freedom and conscience protections remain available (§§92.3, 92.302)
rubrics_metrics.description: Covered entities may rely on Federal religious freedom and conscience protections or seek assurance of exemption under §92.302(b) where applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR revised §92.207(c) to specify nothing in the section precludes a covered entity from availing itself of protections described in §§92.3 and 92.302. Where application of a rule requirement would violate applicable Federal protections for religious freedom and conscience, such application shall not be required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordination with other agencies and applicability of other Federal regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: OCR may coordinate with other regulatory agencies on health insurance-related matters, and covered entities may be subject to other Departmental and Federal regulations governing marketing, EHB, and other aspects of health coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR declined a commenter request to coordinate a specific study of marketing practices but noted ongoing coordination on health insurance-related matters. OCR also referenced CMS EHB nondiscrimination regulations and other Departmental authorities where relevant.
